newsitem.title: TURKEY: Yilmaz in Turkish coalition party talks.
newsitem.headline: Yilmaz in Turkish coalition party talks.

text.p: Turkish prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz was to meet the leaders of four political parties on Tuesday for talks on forming an anti-Islamist coalition, party officials said.
They said Yilmaz was to meet parliament speaker Mustafa Kalemli at 0630 GMT before beginning his talks.
Conservative rival Tansu Ciller's True Path Party (DYP) on Monday rebuffed an invitation by Yilmaz to join his planned coalition.

"The DYP general administration board decided unanimously not to support and not to join any government led by Motherland Party leader Mesut Yilmaz," leading DYP member Mehmet Golhan told a news conference.
Yilmaz and Ciller were nevertheless due to meet later in the day.

Yilmaz is almost assured of the support of two left-wing parties, a right-wing grouping and conservative independents but he is still around a dozen votes short of the simple majority he would need to win a confidence vote.
Investors were confident on Monday that Yilmaz could succeed in replacing Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, who resigned last week but is staying on as caretaker for the time being.
Istanbul shares closed up a solid eight percent on Monday on expectations that free-marketeer Yilmaz could cobble together a coalition from among the squabbling secularist parties.
